title: Domain event envelope
description: Every event written to the outbox and every event delivered to a consumer uses this envelope. Source: phase file 'Events and outbox'. The envelope is versioned independently of the payload it carries.

event_id.description: Unique event identifier. Consumers use this as the idempotency key, so the same event_id must never be reused for a different fact.

event_type.description: Namespaced, past-tense event name. The namespace is the owning module in snake_case; the name states what already happened, never what should happen next.

schema_version.description: Positive integer version of the payload schema for this event_type. Additive optional fields keep the version; anything breaking increments it and requires a dual-read migration.

occurred_at.description: UTC instant at which the fact became true, assigned inside the originating transaction. This is not the publication time.

actor_id.description: Pseudonymous identifier of the actor who caused the change, or null for system-originated events. Never a name, phone number, national ID, or email.

correlation_id.description: Identifier shared by every event and log line originating from one external request.

causation_id.description: event_id of the event that directly caused this one, or null when caused by an external request rather than another event.

tenant.description: Tenant scope for events belonging to a pharmacy organization or branch. Null for events with no tenant dimension.

classification.description: Highest classification present in the payload, per docs/data-classification/classification-policy.md. An event classified 'sensitive' must justify why the identifiers alone were insufficient. 'credential' is not a permitted value: credentials never travel in an event.

payload.description: Minimal, classified facts. Identifiers and the few non-sensitive values a consumer genuinely needs. Never a whole patient, prescription, lab, chat, or AI payload; a consumer that needs more re-reads it from the owning module under its own authorization.
